account:
Today has mostly followed my appointment book: I went to the mill for the morning grain inspection, returned home for lunch, attended the council-letters appointment, took tea with my neighbour, and returned to the office. The inspection remains incomplete because I could not find the miller. My secretary also found nobody at the mill when visiting after three to request another time; no replacement appointment is confirmed. I do not know why the miller was absent.

The unusual feature is repeated, vague talk among townsfolk about a bridge or port change, associated with the bakery and inn. One account mentioned the baker, freight and my neighbour being at the bakery, but I have no firsthand evidence of any actual change or what it would be for. My neighbour said the baker knew of no confirmed changes, and reported seeing nothing unusual along the docks herself. Her definite news was that the baker had stocked his stall and said bread was plentiful. The secretary likewise treats the bridge and port talk as unsubstantiated. It may be circulating gossip; I cannot establish an underlying event or anyone's purpose.

No council letters, urgent matters, or word from the miller have reached the secretary. I have asked that the inspection remain marked incomplete, that a new time be confirmed with the miller, and that correspondence continue to be received. I am at the office with the secretary now, with home scheduled for seven.
